title: Lightning
tldr: When you hear thunder, move into a substantial building or enclosed hard-top vehicle immediately. There is no safe place outdoors during a thunderstorm. Wait at least 30 minutes after the last thunder before going back out.
steps: Get out of water and off ridges, fields and beaches. Do not shelter beneath a lone tree.
Use a building or enclosed hard-top vehicle; picnic shelters and tents are not adequate.
Stay away from showers, sinks, corded phones and plugged-in equipment.
Call emergency services. A lightning victim carries no electrical charge; give CPR if needed and follow dispatcher instructions.
next: Check forecasts before outdoor activity and identify shelter before leaving it.
watch: Lightning can strike beyond rainfall. Do not wait for rain to seek shelter.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Choose a substantial building or enclosed hard-top vehicle now. A tent, tree or open-sided shelter is not protective. If no shelter is available, reduce exposure while moving toward one; there is no outdoor posture that makes lightning safe.
household: Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Decide who helps whom and who carries the essential supplies; do not send a lone child to retrieve items.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, drinking water, a battery light, shoes, phone power and a written contact card within reach. Adapt the load to the hazard and the people with you; do not delay escape to collect equipment.
